title: 10 Reasons to Ignore AI Safety
o: Responses to ten common arguments for dismissing AI safety concerns.
w: HN commenters link it as a compact rebuttal to dismissive arguments and as a way to see why people consider AI safety important.

title: Vibe coding complex changes in Rust
o: See where AI coding agents help and where they fail on a real, complex Rust codebase.
w: Pointed to as a non-promotional, realistic long session of an experienced engineer working with AI on non-trivial code.

title: Karl Sims - Evolved Virtual Creatures, Evolution Simulation, 1994
o: See how evolutionary selection and mutation can design both bodies and controllers of virtual creatures.
w: HN treats it as the classic reference for evolutionary simulation and genetic programming, an inspiration for many projects, with notes on evolution exploiting simulation bugs.

title: Peter Norvig at Startup School 08
o: Hear how Google used large data instead of hand-written rules in projects like image search.
w: HN points to it as a source for Norvig's 'unreasonable effectiveness of data' argument and for his views on image search and the semantic web.

title: Enhancing Photorealism Enhancement
o: Learn how a convolutional network uses rendering buffers to make game frames look photorealistic.
w: Used as a go-to example of neural networks enhancing game rendering, referenced in later AI-graphics discussions.

title: Geoffrey Hinton in conversation with Fei-Fei Li — Responsible AI development
o: Hear two deep learning pioneers recount its history, from ImageNet onward, and debate responsible AI.
w: HN recommends it for Hinton's research history and the two pioneers reflecting on a decade of progress.

title: The Bayesian Trap
o: How Bayes' theorem updates beliefs and how priors can trap reasoning.
w: HN points to it as an accessible introduction to Bayesian reasoning and as inspiration for personal projects.

title: MENACE: the pile of matchboxes which can learn
o: See reinforcement learning work physically as matchboxes learn tic-tac-toe through rewards and punishments.
w: HN cites it as a fun, tangible way to teach machine learning, including to kids.

title: Recent Developments in Deep Learning
o: Learn how deep belief networks stack restricted Boltzmann machines to learn representations layer by layer.
w: Cited as a watchable early introduction to deep learning from its pioneer, and remembered as a mind-blowing moment in the field.

title: Glitch Tokens - Computerphile
o: Understand how tokenizers are trained and why some tokens make GPT models output gibberish.
w: HN points to it as the accessible explanation of why glitch tokens exist whenever tokenizers or odd GPT behavior come up.

title: AI Ethics, Impossibility Theorems and Tradeoffs - Chris Stucchio | Crunch 2018
o: Understand why different fairness criteria for algorithms cannot all be satisfied at once.
w: HN cites it in algorithmic-bias threads for the impossibility result that an algorithm cannot be procedurally fair, group fair and maximally useful at once.

title: John Schulman - Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: Progress and Challenges
o: Understand why RLHF beats behavior cloning for truthfulness and how it relates to hallucination.
w: Recommended in LLM threads as an authoritative explanation from a ChatGPT architect of why models hallucinate and why imitation is not enough.

title: Trends in Deep Learning Hardware: Bill Dally (NVIDIA)
o: Understand where deep learning hardware efficiency comes from: number formats, specialized instructions and energy per operation.
w: HN commenters cite it for NVIDIA's perspective on AI hardware efficiency, including logarithmic number formats and energy use.

title: Cursor Team: Future of Programming with AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #447
o: How an AI code editor integrates custom completion models, speculative edits and context retrieval.
w: HN commenters point to it as the best first-hand account of Cursor's technical internals, straight from its founders.

title: OpenAI's GPT-4 Discussion with Red Teamer Nathan Labenz and Erik Torenberg
o: Learn what red-teaming a frontier model before release involves and what risks it surfaced.
w: Cited as a firsthand account of the raw, unfiltered GPT-4 before safety tuning, especially the part after 45 minutes.

title: Full interview: "Godfather of artificial intelligence" talks impact and potential of AI
o: Hear Hinton explain the history of neural networks and why he thinks LLMs are more than autocomplete.
w: Recommended as a more nuanced look at Hinton's views than headlines, especially his argument that LLMs are more than auto-complete.

title: Why Can't AI Make Its Own Discoveries? — With Yann LeCun
o: LeCun's argument that LLMs lack world models and why that limits discovery.
w: Pointed to as LeCun's argument for the limits of LLMs and the need for world models.

title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence | John Searle | Talks at Google
o: Understand Searle's Chinese room argument that computation alone cannot produce understanding.
w: Used as a source for Searle's own argument in Chinese room discussions, though some find nothing new in it.

title: Geoffrey Hinton talk "What is wrong with convolutional neural nets ?"
o: Understand Hinton's critique of pooling in CNNs and the motivation for capsule networks.
w: Recommended as Hinton's own explanation of capsule networks and his critique of pooling in CNNs.

title: Backpropagation calculus | Deep Learning Chapter 4
o: Derive backpropagation with the chain rule, linking intuition to textbook notation.
w: Recommended as an accessible, visual way to understand backpropagation and neural networks.

title: Solving Wordle using information theory
o: Understand entropy and expected information by building a Wordle solver that picks the most informative guess.
w: HN recommends it as the go-to explanation of optimal Wordle openers like CRANE and a friendly introduction to information theory, also relevant to Mastermind.

title: Lecture 1 | Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition
o: The history and core challenges of computer vision leading up to ImageNet and CNNs.
w: HN recommends the CS231n lectures as a solid, applied deep learning course for self-study.

title: ChatGPT with Rob Miles - Computerphile
o: Understand how human-feedback training shapes ChatGPT and why it produces confident nonsense.
w: HN commenters send it to people confused about ChatGPT's quirks, explaining how human-feedback training makes it a pleasing yes-man that bullshits.

title: The Art Of Poison-Pilling Music Files
o: Understand how adversarial noise can poison audio files against AI training and scraping.
w: HN points to it in AI music and data-poisoning threads as the source for this technique.

title: The Lighthill Debate (1973) - part 1 of 6
o: The 1973 debate behind the Lighthill report and the first AI winter.
w: Recommended as a historical look at the AI winter debate and a demolition of the expert systems hype.

title: StatQuest: Histograms, Clearly Explained
o: Read and build histograms to see how data is distributed, and how bin size changes the picture.

title: Machine Learning for Everybody – Full Course
o: Implement classic algorithms like kNN, naive Bayes, logistic regression and SVMs in Python.

title: Deep Learning Crash Course for Beginners
o: Get a broad first map of deep learning concepts: neurons, loss, optimization, and common architectures.

title: Lesson 9: Deep Learning Foundations to Stable Diffusion
o: Understand how Stable Diffusion works: the U-Net, the VAE, text encoders and the denoising process.

title: Lecture 1: Data-Centric AI vs. Model-Centric AI
o: Why improving data quality often beats changing the model, and core data-centric techniques.

title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision with Python and TensorFlow – Complete Course
o: Build and train convolutional image models in TensorFlow for classification and related vision tasks.

title: Open Pretrained Transformers - Susan Zhang  | Stanford MLSys #77
o: What went wrong and right when Meta pretrained the 175B-parameter OPT model.

title: Lecture 01: When to Use ML and Course Vision (FSDL 2022)
o: Decide when ML is the right tool and how ML projects move from prototype to production.

title: Lecture 1: Deep Learning Fundamentals (Full Stack Deep Learning - Spring 2021)
o: Neural network fundamentals: universal approximation, loss functions, gradient descent and backprop.

title: MLCB24 - Lecture01 - Introduction
o: Get an overview of how machine learning is applied to problems in computational biology.

title: Building resilient ML Engineering skills
o: Understand how accelerator, network and storage performance each limit real ML training workloads.

title: Lecture 8: Markov Decision Processes (MDPs)
o: Model sequential decisions as Markov decision processes and solve them with value iteration.

title: Lecture 9: Markov Decision Process II
o: Solve Markov decision processes with value iteration and policy iteration.

title: Lecture 10: Reinforcement Learning
o: Learn model-free reinforcement learning, including temporal difference learning and Q-learning.

title: Lecture 11: Reinforcement Learning II
o: Learn model-free RL: Q-learning, exploration versus exploitation, and approximate Q-learning with features.

title: Lecture 16 | Machine Learning (Stanford)
o: Learn MDPs, Bellman equations, value iteration and policy iteration from Andrew Ng's CS229.

title: MIT 6.S094: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Motion Planning
o: Deep Q-learning basics applied to a simulated traffic motion-planning task.

title: Reinforcement Learning, by the Book
o: Understand the RL framework from Sutton and Barto: MDPs, returns, value functions and Bellman equations.

title: Bellman Equations, Dynamic Programming, Generalized Policy Iteration | Reinforcement Learning Part 2
o: How Bellman equations underpin dynamic programming and generalized policy iteration.

title: Monte Carlo And Off-Policy Methods | Reinforcement Learning Part 3
o: Understand Monte Carlo value estimation and off-policy learning with importance sampling.

title: Temporal Difference Learning (including Q-Learning) | Reinforcement Learning Part 4
o: Understand temporal difference learning, SARSA and Q-learning and how they update value estimates.

title: Lecture 1: Review Part 1
o: Review the probability foundations needed for statistical machine learning at graduate level.

title: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Self-Taught Learning and Unsupervised Feature Learning
o: Understand the early idea of learning features from unlabeled data with deep networks.

title: Yann LeCun - The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Deep Learning
o: Understand why convolutional networks and learned features beat hand-engineered pipelines in vision.

title: Deep Learning of Representations
o: Bengio on why deep architectures learn useful distributed representations.

title: Principles of Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM): Foundations of Machine Intelligence
o: Understand Numenta's Hierarchical Temporal Memory, a brain-inspired alternative theory of machine intelligence.

title: Machine Learning Discussion Group - Deep Learning w/ Stanford AI Lab (1 of 3)
o: Understand the deep learning basics and unsupervised feature learning as taught around 2013.

title: Adam Coates -- Demystifying Unsupervised Feature Learning -- UC Berkeley 12/7/2012
o: Understand how unsupervised feature learning, such as k-means features, was used to learn image representations.

title: Visual Perception with Deep Learning
o: LeCun on convolutional networks and learned features for visual recognition.

title: Deep Learning: Intelligence from Big Data
o: Hear an early view of deep learning's promise as data and compute grew.

title: Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks and Deep Learning
o: Understand what artificial neurons and layers are and how a neural network learns.

title: Artificial Neural Networks Demystified
o: Understand neurons, layers, activations and how a network learns weights by gradient descent.

title: Architecture of a Modern CNN: the design pattern approach
o: Recognize the recurring design patterns (stem, blocks, head) in modern CNN architectures.

title: A friendly introduction to deep reinforcement learning
o: Understand states, rewards, value functions and how neural networks enable deep Q-learning.

title: What are GANs and how do they work?
o: Understand how a generator and discriminator compete in a GAN to produce realistic data.

title: Coding a basic WGAN in PyTorch
o: Implement a basic Wasserstein GAN in PyTorch, including the critic and its training loop.

title: Lecture 1: Introduction
o: Learn what AI is, its history, and the rational-agent view that frames an intro AI course.

title: ROC Curves and Area Under the Curve (AUC) Explained
o: Read ROC curves and AUC to evaluate a classifier across decision thresholds.

title: VC Dimension
o: Understand VC dimension as a measure of model capacity and its link to overfitting.

title: Weka Tutorial 26: Semi-supervised Learning (Learning Techniques)
o: Run semi-supervised learning on partly labeled data using Weka.

title: AI Fundamentals Builders Need to Know to Fix LLM Limitations
o: Understand LLM limitations and the techniques builders use to work around them, like RAG and fine-tuning.

title: How to Deploy a Machine Learning Model to Google Cloud for 20% Software Engineers (CS329s tutorial)
o: Deploy a trained machine learning model behind an API on Google Cloud.

title: What are Ethics and Why do they Matter? Machine Learning Edition
o: Understand why ethics matters in machine learning, with real cases of harm from deployed systems.

title: An Approach to Data Quality for Netflix Personalization Systems
o: See how Netflix detects data quality problems that break personalization models in production.

title: Zipline: Airbnb’s Machine Learning Data Management Platform - Nikhil Simha and Varant Zanoyan
o: How Airbnb's Zipline computes consistent features for ML training and serving.

title: Zipline - A Declarative Feature Engineering Framework
o: See how Airbnb builds a declarative feature engineering framework for ML in production.

title: Fact Store at Scale for Netflix Recommendations (Nitin Sharma & Kedar Sadekar)
o: Understand how a fact store logs features at scale to train Netflix recommendation models.

title: The Architecture That Powers Twitter's Feature Store | Brittany Wills, Twitter
o: How Twitter's feature store shares features across ML models in production.

title: Automatic Forecasting using Prophet, Databricks, Delta Lake and MLflow
o: See how Atlassian automated time-series forecasting with Prophet and tracked models with MLflow.

title: Uber Practitioner Session
o: See how Uber approaches Bayesian time series forecasting in production with its Orbit package.

title: Daria Sorokina - Amazon Search: The Joy of Ranking Products - MLconf SF 2016
o: Understand how Amazon search uses learning to rank, features and training data to rank products.

title: Productionizing Deep Reinforcement Learning with Spark and MLflow
o: Learn how Zynga trains and serves deep reinforcement learning models in production with Spark and MLflow.

title: Preventing Abuse Using Unsupervised Learning
o: See how LinkedIn uses unsupervised learning to detect fake accounts and abuse at scale.

title: Real-time Machine Learning Inference Platform at Zomato
o: Understand how Zomato serves ML models in real time and the platform choices behind it.

title: Learning Dexterity
o: See how a robot hand learned dexterous manipulation in simulation with domain randomization and RL.

title: Training an unbeatable AI in Trackmania
o: See how a reinforcement learning agent is trained to drive, including reward and design choices.
w: Recommended as an approachable explanation of how reinforcement learning works in practice, and cited for the constraints needed to stop exploits.

title: Autonomous Car - what goes into sensing for autonomous driving?
o: Why Mobileye decomposes self-driving perception instead of training one end-to-end network.
w: Recommended as an accessible technical explanation of Mobileye's approach, and also cited in disputes over Tesla Autopilot.

title: CS231n Winter 2016: Lecture1: Introduction and Historical Context
o: Get the history and scope of computer vision that motivates convolutional neural networks.
w: HN lists it as a free, brilliant introduction to deep learning and computer vision, often within ML self-study plans.

title: Max Tegmark: The Case for Halting AI Development | Lex Fridman Podcast #371
o: Understand the safety-advocate case for pausing giant AI experiments and the risks it targets.
w: Recommended in AI-risk threads as a way to understand the safety-advocate argument for halting development.

title: The Lighthill debate on Artificial Intelligence: "The general purpose robot is a mirage"
o: See the 1973 debate that led to the first AI winter and how early AI was argued over.
w: HN cites it as primary-source history of AI hype and skepticism, and for the vintage Freddy robot footage.

title: Building Brains to Understand the World's Data
o: Hawkins' theory of the neocortex and sparse distributed representations as a path to AI.
w: Recommended as Hawkins' own accessible statement of his brain-inspired theory of intelligence and its software implementation.

title: Yann Lecun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #416
o: Hear Yann LeCun's case for the limits of LLMs and alternative paths toward more capable AI.
w: Cited for LeCun's views on LLM limits and alternative approaches to intelligence.

title: Darts in Higher Dimensions (with 3blue1brown) - Numberphile
o: Build intuition for high-dimensional geometry by computing probabilities with volumes of hyperspheres.
w: Used as a friendly example of high-dimensional geometry showing up in a simple problem, and of ball volume shrinking inside a hypercube.

title: Jim Keller - Moore's Law in the age of AI Chips
o: How scalar, vector and GPU-style parallel computation compare for AI chips.
w: Cited in hardware threads as a Keller talk on the different ways of doing parallel processing.

title: Can we build AI without losing control over it? | Sam Harris
o: Follow the basic argument for why superhuman AI could pose a risk of losing control.
w: HN cites it in AI risk debates, sometimes as an argument that has aged well and sometimes as an example of alarmist framing.

title: Eliezer Yudkowsky: Dangers of AI and the End of Human Civilization | Lex Fridman Podcast #368
o: Understand the strongest pessimistic argument that unaligned superintelligent AI could end human civilization.
w: Mostly cited as the canonical statement of AI doomer views, with some recommending it and many criticizing it as irresponsible or wrong.

title: GradIEEEnt half decent: The hidden power of imprecise lines
o: Why networks need nonlinearity, shown by using floating-point rounding as the activation function.
w: Cited as a fun, unconventional example of neural networks built from floating point error.

title: Deep Visualization Toolbox
o: See what individual units in a convolutional network respond to, from edges to faces.
w: HN points to it as an intuitive way to see what hidden layers of a convnet learn, and as a reference for hierarchical feature learning.

title: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75
o: Understand AIXI, Solomonoff induction and the idea of intelligence as compression.
w: Referenced as an accessible explanation of Kolmogorov complexity and Hutter's view of intelligence as compression.

title: How We Prevent the AI’s from Killing us with Paul Christiano
o: Understand the alignment problem and possible solutions from alignment researcher Paul Christiano.
w: HN links it as a balanced, full-length interview with a leading alignment researcher on AI risk.

title: Correlation CAN Imply Causation! | Statistics Misconceptions
o: Understand how causal models let you infer causation from correlation in data.
w: HN people link it as a short, accessible summary of Judea Pearl-style causal inference when someone repeats that correlation cannot imply causation.

title: The Strange Math That Predicts (Almost) Anything
o: Understand Markov chains, how they were discovered, and how they underpin modern prediction algorithms.
w: HN recommends it as an excellent, detailed history of Markov chains, often in threads on Markov models and language models.

title: Andrej Karpathy: Software Is Changing (Again)
o: Karpathy's Software 1.0/2.0/3.0 framing and how to build partial-autonomy LLM apps.
w: HN mostly cites it as a source for Karpathy's framing of programming in English and his generate-then-verify workflow, with a few critics finding it hype.

title: Visualizing Data Using t-SNE
o: Learn how t-SNE maps high-dimensional data to 2D and how it compares with other methods.
w: HN people point to it as the canonical explanation from the method's author whenever t-SNE comes up.

title: Ch(e)at GPT? - Computerphile
o: Understand how biasing token choices watermarks LLM text so it can later be statistically detected.
w: Linked as the approachable explanation whenever HN discusses detecting or watermarking AI-generated text.

title: Did We Just Change Animation Forever?
o: See how fine-tuned Stable Diffusion models turn filmed footage into consistent anime-style video.
w: HN cites it as an example of temporally stable AI video stylization built from ordinary production gear.

title: Intelligence is not Enough | Bryan Cantrill | Monktoberfest 2023
o: A skeptical engineer's case that intelligence alone does not make AI an existential threat.
w: Recommended as a thoughtful Cantrill talk on embracing failure and curiosity in engineering, and as a skeptical counterpoint to AI doom narratives.

title: Richard Feynman: Can Machines Think?
o: Feynman's 1985 view on whether machines can think and how to define intelligence.
w: HN uses it as an early authoritative take in debates about AI, reasoning, and AGI.

title: But how do AI images and videos actually work? | Guest video by Welch Labs
o: Understand how CLIP embeddings, diffusion sampling and classifier-free guidance produce AI images and video.
w: HN uses it as a clear explainer for diffusion mechanics, such as negative prompts and faster sampling, and for joint text-image encoders.

title: Multi-Agent Hide and Seek
o: See how multi-agent self-play produces emergent strategies and tool use without being programmed.
w: HN uses it as a vivid example of emergent behavior from multi-agent reinforcement learning, and as a way to make AI misalignment concerns feel concrete.

title: Human AI is Decades Away, But We Need to Start the Debate Now | Demis Hassabis | Google Zeitgeist
o: Hear DeepMind's early vision of general AI built through game-playing agents.
w: HN cites it for the DeepMind CEO's early views on AI and its game-playing focus, in AlphaGo and OpenAI threads.

title: Ken Stanley: Discovery Without Objectives
o: Why objective-free novelty search can find solutions that direct optimization misses.
w: Cited as a source for the idea that open-ended search can beat objective-driven optimization, though one commenter found parts of it fluffy.

title: Jeff Dean & Noam Shazeer — 25 years at Google: from PageRank to AGI
o: Hear how key Google researchers see the path from PageRank to transformers, mixture of experts and AGI.
w: HN cites it for insight into Google researchers' views on AI progress and publishing, though one commenter finds the interview weak.

title: Building the Software 2 0 Stack (Andrej Karpathy)
o: Understand Software 2.0: neural networks trained on curated data replacing hand-written code.
w: HN uses it as the primary source for the 'Software 2.0' idea and recommends it as a quick talk on the next software stack.

title: We Were Right! Real Inner Misalignment
o: Understand inner misalignment and goal misgeneralization through real RL experiments that demonstrate them.
w: Pointed to as evidence that AI misalignment is an empirically demonstrated problem, for people who dismiss it.
